outputs: Synthetic text instances with labels for text classification
Synthetic text instances for training text classification models

changes_made.explanation: Removed duplicate dataset entries (case variations) and consolidated task description. The paper focuses on synthetic data generation, not data augmentation as a separate task.

Removed data diversity metrics (Remote Clique Score, Chamfer Distance Score) and similarity metrics (Cosine Similarity) as they are not used to evaluate generated NLG outputs, but rather to analyze data characteristics. Only kept classification evaluation metrics (Macro-F1, Accuracy) that are used to evaluate models trained on the synthetic data.
No LLM-as-judge evaluation is conducted in this paper. The LLM (GPT-3.5-Turbo) is used only for generation, not for evaluation.

guideline: workers were asked to determine which text classification task in the pair was more objective, with "objectivity" of a task defined as "the classification of a piece of text is based on clear, identifiable features in the text (e.g., keywords or phrases), and can be done without being affected by any personal interpretation of the text resulted from personal biases, emotions or beliefs."

changes_made.explanation: Human evaluations were conducted to assess task subjectivity and collect instance-level annotations, but NOT to evaluate the generated NLG outputs. The human judgments were used to characterize the datasets/tasks, not to evaluate the quality of the synthetic text generated by the LLM.

overall_notes: This paper studies synthetic data generation using LLMs for text classification tasks, but does NOT evaluate the quality of the generated text itself. The evaluation focuses on how well models trained on synthetic data perform on classification tasks, not on evaluating the generated text quality. Human evaluations were conducted to characterize task subjectivity, not to evaluate NLG outputs. The paper is more about data generation than NLG evaluation per se.
